data.description:
# W3 — Resize the Gerrit host t4g.large -> r7g.large (2 vCPU, 8 GiB -> 2 vCPU, 16 GiB)

Implements workstream **W3** of parent epic `couped-subzero-wolf` ("Right-size or change
instance family"), which that epic explicitly records as an **operator decision because it
costs money**. The operator has approved r7g.large and **capped the change at r7g.large's
cost**; larger types are out of scope by that approval and must not be proposed here.

## Context / Problem

The sibling story `cryptozoic-unlit-ladybug` (the $0 half) sizes four per-service container
memory limits from measured steady state. Those four limits do not fit the current host:

```
gerrit 3072 + mcp 3655 + review-bot 1343 + opcert 256  =  9088 MiB
host total (measured `free -m`, 2026-09-06 01:29 UTC)  =  7813 MiB
                                                          ------
                                                          OVER by 1275 MiB
```

MCP alone measures **2.87 GiB** steady state (post-change-2685, recorded on the epic under
AC6), i.e. 38% of the present box. So the $0 half is arithmetically unlandable as sized on a
7,813 MiB host: something must either shrink below its measured demand or the host must grow.
This ticket grows the host to 16 GiB, which leaves the 9,088 MiB limit sum roughly 42% of
headroom on a 16,384 MiB machine.

## Why r7g.large, and why CPU deliberately does NOT change

| type | vCPU | MiB | on-demand/mo | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| t4g.large (current) | 2 | 8192 | $49.06 | memory-starved |
| **r7g.large** | 2 | 16384 | $78.18 | **approved ceiling** |
| c7g.xlarge | 4 | 8192 | $105.85 | over the approval, and does not fix memory |
| m7g.xlarge | 4 | 16384 | $119.14 | over the approval |

The binding constraint is **memory, not CPU**. The peak load average of 5.08 recorded on the
epic was measured while SIX heavyweight consumers ran concurrently (three `make verify` runs
from separate worktrees plus three `review-plan` gates) against a 4-slot semaphore — that is
unbounded concurrency, which `cryptozoic-unlit-ladybug` is separately fixing, not steady
demand. Sustained demand measured ~1.1 vCPU; current load 0.74. So this ticket holds vCPU at
2 and buys only RAM. Any argument for more vCPU belongs in a separate ticket and is the
operator's cost decision.

r7g is also **not burstable**, which additionally discharges the concern in
`relevant-dissident-salamander` (t4g CPU credit balance pinned at zero since 12:38Z, running
on billed surplus): a non-burstable family has no credit balance to exhaust. That is a
side-effect of this change, not its justification, and that bug is not closed by this ticket.

## Why this is AMI-compatible (the risk that would break the host)

`infra/terraform/main.tf:12-14` resolves the AMI from the public SSM parameter
`/aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-arm64` — an **arm64** image —
and `main.tf:97` pins it with `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [ami] }`. An instance type whose
architecture is not arm64 would produce an instance that cannot boot. r7g is Graviton3, i.e.
arm64, so the swap is architecture-preserving. This must be **verified with the API**, not
asserted from the name, before the change is pushed (AC2).

## What changes

Exactly one default, plus the description that documents its arm64 constraint:

- `infra/terraform/variables.tf:7-11` — `variable "instance_type"` default
  `"t4g.large"` -> `"r7g.large"`, and its description updated so the sentence naming the
  Graviton/arm64 constraint still names the type that is actually configured.

No other terraform resource changes. `aws_instance.gerrit` (`main.tf:67-104`) reads
`var.instance_type` and needs no edit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 `infra/terraform/variables.tf` declares `instance_type` default `"r7g.large"`, and
      its `description` states the arm64/Graviton constraint in terms of `r7g.large` (no
      surviving reference to `t4g.large` as the configured type). Verified by
      `grep -n 'r7g.large' infra/terraform/variables.tf` returning both the default and the
      description line, and `grep -c 't4g' infra/terraform/variables.tf` returning 0.
- [ ] AC2 r7g.large is proven arm64 and available in the instance's AZ from the AWS API, not
      from the type name. Verified by
      `aws ec2 describe-instance-types --instance-types r7g.large --query
      'InstanceTypes[].ProcessorInfo.SupportedArchitectures'` returning `["arm64"]`, and
      `aws ec2 describe-instance-type-offerings --location-type availability-zone --filters
      Name=instance-type,Values=r7g.large Name=location,Values=us-east-1a` returning that AZ.
      The AMI the config selects is confirmed arm64 by
      `aws ec2 describe-images --image-ids $(aws ssm get-parameter --name
      /aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-arm64 --query
      Parameter.Value --output text) --query 'Images[].Architecture'`.
- [ ] AC3 `terraform plan` GENERATES (exit 0 or 2, never 1, no `Error:` line) and shows
      `aws_instance.gerrit` as **`will be updated in-place`** with **`0 to destroy`** and no
      `forces replacement` / `must be replaced` anywhere in the output. An instance-type
      change on an EBS-backed instance is a stop/modify/start, not a replacement; a plan
      saying otherwise means STOP, because a replacement would destroy the Gerrit host.
      Verified by the recorded plan transcript on this ticket.
- [ ] AC4 The pre-existing drift the plan carries (unrelated adds/changes from earlier
      unapplied work) is enumerated in a comment on this ticket, so the operator's Phase-2
      apply is not a surprise. This ticket does NOT attempt to reconcile that drift.
- [ ] AC5 The repo's existing test suite still passes and no test pins the instance type. A
      sweep for an infra-invariant test covering instance sizing is recorded: if one exists it
      is updated, and if none exists that is stated rather than a new one being invented.
      Verified by `grep -rn 't4g\|instance_type' tests/` and `make verify`.
- [ ] AC6 The change lands through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`. The apply is
      NOT performed as part of this change: it is a separate, operator-authorised step taken
      only after the change merges.

## Apply plan (Phase 2, operator-gated — recorded here so it is reviewable, not executed by this change)

1. EBS snapshots of both attached volumes (root + gerrit data) taken and their ids recorded
   on this ticket BEFORE the apply.
2. `terraform apply`. This **stops and starts the instance**: expect a Gerrit outage of
   roughly 3 minutes (a prior stop/start on this host ran 23:51:25 -> 23:54:17). That is
   expected behaviour, not a fault.
3. Post-apply verification, all recorded on this ticket:
   - all four containers healthy (`gerrit`, `mcp`, `review-bot`, `opcert`). Watch
     **review-bot** specifically: every container uses `unless-stopped`, and a container that
     `Exited (0)` does NOT restart across a host stop/start — that silently killed the
     `LLM-Review` vote source for 59 minutes earlier this session, which is the exact failure
     `complex-sassy-blackfly` records.
   - `free -m` reports ~16 GiB total.
   - the gate-scratch volume is still mounted at `var.gate_scratch_mount`
     (`/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`). It is fstab-by-UUID with `nofail`, so it should survive,
     but `nofail` is precisely what makes a silent fallback to the root filesystem possible.
     Verified with `mountpoint -q` + `findmnt`, and by confirming the two markers sit on
     DIFFERENT devices (`stat -c %d /var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required` vs
     `stat -c %d /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted`) — the check story
     `injurious-wellmade-moth` established.
   - Gerrit answers HTTP 200 and `git ls-remote` succeeds.
   - no NEW CloudWatch alarms attributable to the resize.

## Risks and how each is handled

- **Replacement instead of in-place modify** — would destroy the host. Caught by AC3 before
  any apply; the plan is read, not assumed.
- **Architecture mismatch** — would produce an unbootable instance. Caught by AC2 against the
  API before the change is pushed.
- **Gate-scratch volume not remounting** — would undo `injurious-wellmade-moth` and return
  gate scratch to the root filesystem silently. Caught by the two-marker different-device
  check in the Phase-2 verification.
- **review-bot not restarting** — would silently remove the `LLM-Review` gate. Explicitly
  checked in Phase-2 verification.
- **Cost** — +$29.12/mo over t4g.large. This is the approved figure and the approved ceiling.

## Not in scope

Instance family changes above r7g.large's cost; the container memory limits themselves (that
is `cryptozoic-unlit-ladybug`); reconciling the pre-existing terraform drift; closing
`relevant-dissident-salamander`.
